learning: If slalom line_loss_events is 0 and slalom max_error is below 0.06 m, the lead was the trigger and 0.067 m is the working row. If line loss stays at 1 on slalom, the lead is not the trigger at this speed, and the next lever is the controller, not geometry. Slalom oscillation has stayed at 0.13 to 0.14 across all rows tested, so a kd change is the next controller test if oscillation stays above 0.10.
notes: Package for the y=0.067 m row with the ±0.065 m, 16 mm layout from iteration 8. The controller is unchanged from iteration 8 so the race isolates the 3 mm lead reduction.
rationale: Iteration 8 is the best raced design (56.40): the ±0.065 m spread cut s-bend line loss to 0.05 per run and gave s-bend progress 0.1825. Slalom still lost the line once per run (max_error 0.0604 m, oscillation 0.131). Iterations 3, 4 and 5 show that slalom oscillation stays near 0.13 to 0.14 at every row position (y=0.05 to 0.07 m), so the lead is not its cause. Iteration 7 (y=0.065 m, ±0.065 m) lost the slalom line and fell back to s-bend progress 0.04, so the lead should not drop far below 0.067 m. I accept the Builder's geometry as written: the same ±0.065 m, 16 mm layout as iteration 8, with the forward row moved to y=0.067 m. The controller is kept exactly as in iteration 8 (kp 2.0, ki 0, kd 0.10, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]). Changing the controller in the same race would make the row result impossible to attribute, and kd and kp have not been shown to move slalom oscillation. The observation request asks for per-track line loss, max_error, progress and oscillation so the slalom and s-bend results can be read separately. Expected: slalom line loss near 0, s-bend progress near 0.18, and a score of 53 to 58. Risk: the 3 mm lead cut may lose some s-bend progress.
